binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable space, a measure μ on Ω, and the assumption that μ is a probability measure.
A natural number N together with hN: 0<N.
A family X=(X_i) indexed by i∈Fin N, where each X_i: Ω→ℝ.
hypotheses: Every X_i belongs to L²(μ), i.e. is square-integrable.
The family is pairwise independent: X_i and X_j are independent under μ whenever i≠j.
Every X_i has the same distribution under μ as the distinguished variable X_0.
4σ²/ε²≤N, where N is regarded as a real number.
conclusions: The real-valued μ-measure of the event {|N⁻¹∑_{i∈Fin N}X_i−∫X_0 dμ|≥ε} is at most 1/4.
mathematical_definitions: The distinguished index 0 is valid because N>0.
The sample mean is N⁻¹ times the finite sum of X_i over all i∈Fin N.
The centering constant ∫X_0 dμ is the common expectation supplied by identical distribution and square integrability.
The deviation event uses a non-strict threshold: absolute deviation greater than or equal to ε.
Measure.real converts μ of the event from an extended nonnegative real to a real; as μ is a probability measure, this event measure is finite.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For N>0 pairwise independent, identically distributed, measurable, square-integrable real random variables on a probability space, if their common variance is σ², ε is positive, and N is at least 4σ²/ε², then the probability that their sample mean differs from their common expectation by at least ε is at most one quarter.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The family is assumed only pairwise independent, not mutually or jointly independent.
All variables are real-valued and the index set is the finite nonempty type Fin N.
Identical distribution is stated relative to X_0, whose existence depends on the explicit hypothesis N>0.
σ is not required to be nonnegative; only σ² appears, so replacing σ by -σ makes no difference.
The theorem is conditional on 4σ²/ε²≤N. When that inequality is false, the implication has no applicable instance rather than asserting a weaker probability bound.
ε is explicitly positive, so division by ε² is nondegenerate.
The bad event includes equality at the threshold because the comparison is ≥ε, not >ε.
The conclusion is centered at the expectation of X_0; no zero-mean assumption is present.
The proposition gives the fixed numerical bound 1/4 and does not itself state the more general Chebyshev bound σ²/(Nε²).
